findings: S34: (a) appearance captures may be placed+cached; (b) arrival captures may not. Settle proof mandatory.

MEASURED: the province streamer is pumped ONLY from engine.teleport() and engine._applyCell(); sim/step.js never touches renderer.province. So a camera posed where the player has never been looks at an EMPTY world forever, and two frames 12 apart are BYTE-IDENTICAL. Naive 'two stable frames = settled' passes a photograph of nothing. 5/5 'absent' controls: changed_frac=0.000000 with 19-25 tiles unbuilt. IMAGE STABILITY ALONE IS NOT A SUFFICIENT SETTLE GATE.

MEASURED: this world is ALIVE. A legitimately settled frame moves up to 8.7% of pixels / 20% of 24px blocks in 12 frames (ground cover sway, ashfall, rain, water). Naive two-frame stability CANNOT separate settled from streaming at any block size (separated=false for px,b4,b8,b12,b24,b48).

SOLUTION: three frames A(t),B(t+12),C(t+24). excess = max(0, d(A,B) - d(B,C)) subtracts the scene's own ambient-motion floor. At 4x4 blocks of a 384x216 thumbnail, delta>8/255: settled excess <= 0.00251 (n=13), streaming excess in [0.01157, 0.1412] (n=5). CLEAN BAND. Threshold 0.005 (2.0x margin below, 2.3x above).
MEASURED: lighting converges in ONE frame in this build (noon->01:00 + storm, zero settle frames: excess=0 in 5/5). G3 has no lighting-convergence case to catch here.
Gates: G1 residency (streamAround(x,z,0).queued must be 0 -- budget 0 builds nothing so it is a pure read), G2 quiescence (built==0 && tilesQueued==0), G3 stability (excess <= 0.005).
boot-check baseline: PASS in 13.6 s. Box load ~6 on 4 cores at start.
The 117-frame pack is tools/world/province-shots.mjs: 13 regions x 3 per x 3 passes (day,night,worst).
MEASURED end-to-end: cold start (spawn daemon + boot browser + 1 capture) 10.2-15.4 s. Warm cache MISS at 1280x720: 0.86-0.94 s. Cache HIT: 12-13 ms in-daemon, 93 ms wall incl. node startup.

PERF TRAP FOUND AND FIXED: marshalling a 384x216 RGBA thumbnail out of the page as a JSON array (~330k numbers) cost ~2 s per frame - MORE than the render it measures. Warm capture was 7.0 s. Moving the block-mean diff in-page (__CAPD_SNAP/__CAPD_DIFF, only aggregates cross CDP) took it to 0.86 s. 8x.

Daemon: unix socket reports/runs/.capture/capd.sock, O_EXCL lock file for race-free idempotent start, per-connection FIFOs with round-robin scheduling for fairness, build stat-signature watch, two-stage idle (browser 180 s / daemon 1800 s).

FALSIFICATION: 10/10 attacks repelled. A1 unstreamed -> refused (G1 queued=23 unbuilt tiles). A2a-f six arrival-laundering variants -> all ARRIVAL_REFUSED. A3 control -> succeeds (so the refusals are not a service that refuses everything). A4 provenance -> 11/11 fields. A5 cache integrity -> hit in 7 ms with the same sha256 and full provenance.

TEST-DESIGN BUG FOUND IN MY OWN FALSIFIER: the 'park the player far away' step was served FROM CACHE, so it never moved the world and the A1 target was still resident. A cache hit never touches the browser - that is the point of the cache - so any test that relies on a side effect of a capture must pass no_cache:true.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED: tools/lib/browser.mjs handle.h() ends a harness error with die() -> process.exit(). In a shared daemon one bad pose from one client killed the browser for everyone. Server now uses a non-fatal hx()/hxOpt().

BUG FOUND AND FIXED: canonicalSpec emitted camera.dir/up as null; __HARNESS.camera() rejects unknown pose keys outright (engine.js:3345), so every explicit camera pose failed. Now only set keys are emitted.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED: launchGame() reports failure via die() -> process.exit(), so a game/ that does not boot killed the daemon in a respawn loop. Boot now runs with process.exit swapped for a throw; failure becomes a GAME_BROKEN job error with a 15 s backoff and the daemon stays up.

ADDED --pin-build: measured during the headline run, another builder edited game/ FOUR TIMES IN THREE MINUTES; the daemon correctly dropped the browser and invalidated the cache each time, which makes a 117-frame pack a mixture of four different games. Pinning freezes the build key for the pack and records build_pinned + tree_has_since_moved_to.

ENVIRONMENT: at 10:41 UTC another builder's in-flight edit left game/ throwing at boot (_assertGiversAreVisibleToRace: 19 quest givers with no NPC record, 13 with no reaction_group). boot-check FAILS for that reason, which is not mine. Must be re-checked when they finish.

The headline benchmark is therefore measured in an isolated git worktree at 5526173 (the last bootable commit), with my current tools/ copied in and tools/node_modules symlinked. The working tree was not touched.

SOUNDNESS FIX: a capture's result must depend only on its spec, or the cache promise is false. The daemon now reloads the world before any capture that does not itself say where the player is (no `place`), and after any capture that ran `ops` or opened a menu. A clean place->place sequence (the whole region pack) keeps the fast path.

CONCURRENCY TEST DESIGN: the first draft passed --no-cache to every agent, which made the overlapping requests each render and then pass the identical-sha256 check for the wrong reason. It now uses a per-run nonce and asserts exactly ONE render + N-1 cache hits among the overlapping group.
BENCHMARK (worktree at 5526173, box load 5-10): CONTROL, the ORIGINAL private-browser path, 13 frames (--per 1 --passes day --direct) = 204 s = 15.7 s/frame including boot.

PHASE BREAKDOWN of a service capture at 1280x720 (from the manifest's phase_ms): settle_ms 12140 (three renders + stepping + two in-page diffs), place_ms 1491 (teleport + province drain), screenshot_ms 271, pose/stream/setup ~7 ms. render_ms total 13647. The SETTLE PROOF is the dominant cost and it is the price S34 sets: three frames instead of one.

The direct path pays 2 renders per frame (stepFrames ends with one renderNow because it never calls setRenderRate(0), plus the explicit renderFrame); the service pays 3 renders but steps for free. Per-frame cost is therefore comparable; the service's win is boot amortisation, the cache, and NOT MULTIPLYING BROWSERS.
Box load during the benchmark was 5-10 on 4 cores (other agents active), so absolute per-frame numbers are load-dependent; the direct control was run in the same window for a fair comparison.
BENCHMARK RESULTS (worktree 5526173, 13 frames = --per 1 --passes day, box load 5-12 on 4 cores):
DIRECT (original private-browser path): 204 s = 15.7 s/frame incl. boot.

SERVICE, COLD CACHE: 285 s = 21.9 s/frame. SLOWER per frame than direct by 40%. HONEST FINDING: the three-frame settle proof S34 demands costs more than the one browser boot it saves, for a single agent doing a cold run. The service's win is NOT per-frame speed.
SERVICE, WARM CACHE: 3 s for the same 13 frames = 0.23 s/frame. 68x faster than direct, 95x faster than the cold service run.

CORRECTNESS: the batched sampler (chunked candidates + PRNG state rewind) reproduces the direct path's 13 sampled points EXACTLY - identical region/x/z/yaw/weather/hours for all 13, and identical reshot counts. Routing through the service did not change what the pack photographs.
All 13 service frames settled=true, arrival=placed.

FALSIFICATION re-run on the final code: THE GATES HOLD, 10/10 attacks repelled. A1 unstreamed refused in 10.5 s (G1 queued=21 unbuilt tiles). A2a-f all ARRIVAL_REFUSED. A3 control captured, settled. A4 11/11 provenance fields. A5 cache hit 55 ms, identical sha256.

MEASUREMENT FLAW FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN TESTS: browserCount() counts every browser on the box, and this box is SHARED - 24 browser processes belonging to other agents were live mid-run. An assertion of 'exactly one browser on the box' would fail for reasons unrelated to the service. Both concurrency-test and contention-test now assert on the DELTA from their own baseline.

CONCURRENCY MEASURED: 6 separate client PROCESSES started at once against a COLD daemon. Browser count on the box went 5 -> peak 6: DELTA EXACTLY 1. All 6 succeeded. Of the 3 agents asking for the SAME picture, 1 rendered it and 2 were served it from cache, 1 distinct sha256. N agents did not become N browsers, and overlapping work was done once.

RACE BUG FOUND IN MY OWN START PATH, BY ITS OWN LOG, AND FIXED. The first version used an O_EXCL lock file as the rendezvous and judged a lock stale when the holder's pid was alive but its socket did not yet answer - which is exactly the window between taking the lock and finishing listen(). capd.log shows FOUR processes logging 'listening on' within 300 ms when six agents raced. Fix: listen() on a unix socket path IS the atomic operation (the kernel lets one process bind), so the bind is now the exclusion and the lock file only serialises removing a CORPSE socket file. VERIFIED: 8 daemons launched simultaneously produced exactly 1 'listening on' line and 1 daemon.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE RACE BUG, observed live: three orphaned daemons from the losing side of the race stayed alive with their own browsers and logged their own idle-closes into the shared capd.log, which is what makes the bug expensive rather than merely untidy. They were killed by hand; with the bind-as-exclusion fix they cannot occur. The CONCURRENCY.json produced by this run was measured against the OLD start path and should be re-run.

SECOND BUG FROM THE SAME CLEANUP: shutdown() unlinked the socket unconditionally, so killing a LOSING daemon removed the LIVE daemon's socket out from under a 40-frame job. Fixed: only the process that actually bound the socket (I_OWN_SOCKET, set inside bindExclusive) may unlink it. General lesson: a process must not clean up a resource it does not own.

RACE FIX CONFIRMED UNDER THE REAL WORKLOAD: with the bind-as-exclusion start path, 6 client processes racing a cold daemon produced exactly ONE 'booting browser' line and four 'another capture daemon already owns ... - exiting' lines, and exactly one server process survived. Before the fix the same race produced four processes all logging 'listening on'.
